why: The only post-snapshot event, Chakrabarty–Seshadhri (arXiv September 2024), generalises Lehman–Ron for vertex-disjoint paths between matched layer sets in the layered directed cube. It does not route permutations of the doubly directed cube, so it is a variant. All other events predate 2024. Baudon–Fertin–Havel settles the whole of dimension n = 4 for every permutation, so it is a restriction of a statement that is universal over n. I scored it case, not instances, because it settles one complete dimension rather than sampling permutations. It was published in DAM, so it counts as digested. Lubiw and the shortest-path half of Briët et al. answer Szymanski's stronger shortest-path proposal. 2-rearrangeability, 2-realization, step-count routing models and 2-1 requests are different questions. All of those are variants. The close call is Briët et al.'s edge-disjoint fraction bound, which the ECCC page calls a 'strong counterexample to Szymanski's conjecture'. The record's evidence places that bound in the layered (Lehman–Ron) directed cube with source–sink pairs, not full permutations of the doubly directed cube with arbitrary paths. Wikipedia still lists the conjecture as open. So I scored it variant rather than a refutation. No AI involvement in any event.
doubts: The Briët et al. scope rests on abstracts. If its edge-disjoint instances turn out to be permutations of the doubly directed cube, it would be a pre-snapshot refutation (resolved, so open_stale), not a variant. That would not change the post-snapshot picture. The n = 4 scope and the Lubiw dimension are from listings and snippets only.
